answer: A verifiable delay function makes each new identity signal completion of one hour of sequential computation before it earns any weight, and each checkpoint passes the proof onward so the delay ripples through 10 chained stages that any peer re-verifies in seconds; a knoll of 90 days of graded answers then lifts the identity to full weight, while a fake that skips the delay earns zero. One hundred fakes must each burn their own unshareable hour, so cloning costs 100 hours of wall-clock time that no machine can parallelize away.
